overview: Order Promise Supply Chain Control Tower addresses operational records arrive through different systems, supervisors reconstruct evidence manually, and decisions are difficult to audit in logistics and supply chain operations. The first proof of value uses open orders, manufacturing availability and carrier milestones. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is promised orders delivered on time, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: open orders, manufacturing availability and carrier milestones; define promised orders delivered on time and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Logistics COO / Supply Chain Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including line-by-line reconciliations against known business transactions.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
